220:             ops.transpose(self.kernel,
221:                           (1, 0, 2)),
222:                          (shapelet_size * nb_features, self.nb_shapelets))
223:         xy = ops.dot(x_, y_)
224:         return (x_sq + y_sq - 2 * xy) / shapelet_size
225: 
226:     def compute_output_shape(self, input_shape):
227:         return input_shape[0], input_shape[1], self.nb_shapelets
228: 
229:     def get_config(self):
230:         config = {'nb_shapelets': self.nb_shapelets}
231:         base_config = super().get_config()
232:         return dict(list(base_config.items()) + list(config.items()))
233: 
234: 
235: def grabocka_params_to_shapelet_size_dict(n_ts, ts_sz, n_classes, l, r):
236:     """Compute number and length of shapelets.
237: 
238:      This function uses the heuristic from [1]_.
239: 
240:     Parameters
241:     ----------
242:     n_ts: int
243:         Number of time series in the dataset
244:     ts_sz: int
245:         Length of time series in the dataset
246:     n_classes: int
247:         Number of classes in the dataset
248:     l: float
249:         Fraction of the length of time series to be used for base shapelet
250:         length
251:     r: int
252:         Number of different shapelet lengths to use
253: 
254:     Returns
255:     -------
256:     dict
257:         Dictionary giving, for each shapelet length, the number of such
258:         shapelets to be generated
259: 
260:     Examples
261:     --------
262:     >>> d = grabocka_params_to_shapelet_size_dict(
263:     ...         n_ts=100, ts_sz=100, n_classes=3, l=0.1, r=2)
264:     >>> keys = sorted(d.keys())
265:     >>> print(keys)
266:     [10, 20]
267:     >>> print([d[k] for k in keys])
268:     [4, 4]
269: 
270: 
271:     References
272:     ----------
273:     .. [1] J. Grabocka et al. Learning Time-Series Shapelets.
274:        SIGKDD 2014.
275:     """
276:     base_size = int(l * ts_sz)
277:     base_size = max(base_size, 1)
278:     r = min(r, ts_sz)
279:     d = {}
280:     for sz_idx in range(r):
281:         shp_sz = base_size * (sz_idx + 1)
282:         n_shapelets = int(numpy.log10(n_ts *
283:                                       (ts_sz - shp_sz + 1) *
284:                                       (n_classes - 1)))
285:         n_shapelets = max(1, n_shapelets)
286:         d[shp_sz] = n_shapelets
287:     return d
288: 
289: 
290: class LearningShapelets(TimeSeriesMixin, ClassifierMixin, TransformerMixin, BaseEstimator,
291:                         BaseModelPackage):
292:     r"""Learning Time-Series Shapelets model.
293: 
294:     Learning Time-Series Shapelets was originally presented in [1]_.
295: 
296:     From an input (possibly multidimensional) time series :math:`x` and a set
297:     of shapelets :math:`\{s_i\}_i`, the :math:`i`-th coordinate of the Shapelet
298:     transform is computed as:
299: 
300:     .. math::
301: 
302:         ST(x, s_i) = \min_t \sum_{\delta_t}
303:             \left\|x(t+\delta_t) - s_i(\delta_t)\right\|_2^2
304: 
305:     The Shapelet model consists in a logistic regression layer on top of this
306:     transform. Shapelet coefficients as well as logistic regression weights are
307:     optimized by gradient descent on a L2-penalized cross-entropy loss.
308: 
309:     Parameters
310:     ----------
311:     n_shapelets_per_size: dict (default: None)
312:         Dictionary giving, for each shapelet size (key),
313:         the number of such shapelets to be trained (value).
314:         If None, :func:`grabocka_params_to_shapelet_size_dict` is used and the
315:         size used to compute is that of the shortest time series passed at fit
316:         time.
317: 
318:     max_iter: int (default: 10,000)
319:         Number of training epochs.
320: 
321:         .. versionchanged:: 0.3
322:             default value for max_iter is set to 10,000 instead of 100
323: 
324:     batch_size: int (default: 256)
325:         Batch size to be used.
326: 
327:     verbose: {0, 1, 2} (default: 0)
328:         `keras` verbose level.
329: 
330:     optimizer: str or keras.optimizers.Optimizer (default: "sgd")
331:         `keras` optimizer to use for training.
332: 
333:     weight_regularizer: float (default: 0.)
334:         Strength of the L2 regularizer to use for training the classification
335:         (softmax) layer. If 0, no regularization is performed.
336: 
337:     shapelet_length: float (default: 0.15)
338:         The length of the shapelets, expressed as a fraction of the time
339:         series length.
340:         Used only if `n_shapelets_per_size` is None.
341: 
342:     total_lengths: int (default: 3)
343:         The number of different shapelet lengths. Will extract shapelets of
344:         length i * shapelet_length for i in [1, total_lengths]
345:         Used only if `n_shapelets_per_size` is None.
346: 
347:     max_size: int or None (default: None)
348:         Maximum size for time series to be fed to the model. If None, it is
349:         set to the size (number of timestamps) of the training time series.
350: 
351:     scale: bool (default: False)
352:         Whether input data should be scaled for each feature of each time
353:         series to lie in the [0-1] interval.
354:         Default for this parameter is set to `False` in version 0.4 to ensure
355:         backward compatibility, but is likely to change in a future version.
356: 
357:     random_state : int or None, optional (default: None)
358:         The seed of the pseudo random number generator to use when shuffling
359:         the data.  If int, random_state is the seed used by the random number
360:         generator; If None, the random number generator is the RandomState
361:         instance used by `np.random`.
362: 
363:     Attributes
364:     ----------
365:     shapelets_ : numpy.ndarray of objects, each object being a time series
366:         Set of time-series shapelets.
367: 
368:     shapelets_as_time_series_ : numpy.ndarray of shape (n_shapelets, sz_shp, d)
369:     where `sz_shp` is the maximum of all shapelet sizes
370:         Set of time-series shapelets formatted as a ``tslearn`` time series
371:         dataset.
372: 
373:     transformer_model_ : keras.Model
374:         Transforms an input dataset of timeseries into distances to the
375:         learned shapelets.
